findings.title: Webhook 'unknown' vs 'unknown order' reason-string drift
findings.problem: The refund-branch no-row case returns reason:'unknown', while the live capture handler (razorpay-webhook.ts) returns reason:'unknown order'. Cosmetic inconsistency within the single handler; body shape {status:'ignored'} is what tests assert.
findings.fix: Keep the capture branch's 'unknown order' string; use a distinct 'unknown payment' for the refund branch rather than a bare 'unknown'.

findings.title: confirmCapture status-recompute change under-scoped
findings.problem: confirmCapture currently writes each allocated charge's status from planAllocation's alloc.nextStatus (nextChargeStatus => PAID/PARTIALLY_PAID only). A concession-zeroed charge is not an allocation target, so capture does not regress it; the change is defensive, not a correctness fix. The design should pin that the allocation loop is otherwise byte-for-byte preserved.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to §E.5: 'no change to the allocation loop; only the status written for an allocated charge is sourced from computeChargeStatus instead of alloc.nextStatus, and a fast confirmation.test.ts regression asserts identical output for the no-credit case.'

findings.title: OQ-1 refund webhook event names/payload path unverifiable in-repo
findings.problem: refund.processed/refund.failed/refund.created and payload.refund.entity come from Razorpay public docs, not the installed SDK (only the payments.refund method and RazorpayRefund entity are verifiable). Accepted pre-go-live confirmation, not a design defect; blast radius isolated to the eventType switch and entity path.
findings.fix: Keep OQ-1 open; confirm event names/path against the live Razorpay dashboard webhook event list before enabling refund webhooks. No code change now.
